title: Service trust covenant and oncall experiment log (cross-functional)
content:
Purpose
This doc creates a lightweight, cross-functional "service trust covenant" — a compact set of commitments and experiment notes to align product, infra, and SRE on service expectations, incident handling, and how we measure success. It is intentionally pragmatic: short commitments, measurable signals, and 30/60/90 experiments we can run with minimal ceremony.

Background
We need a faster way to operationalize contractual expectations between feature teams and SRE without waiting for long-form SLO adoption. The covenant sits between a full SLO formalization and ad-hoc tribal knowledge: enough structure to make trade-offs visible and test operational readiness.

High-level goals
- Reduce P99 tail impact on customer-facing flows by 25% for target services in 90d.
- Ensure every new feature has an owner who signs the covenant before rollout.
- Run three lightweight oncall experiments to test escalation handoffs and automated mitigations.

Signals and metrics (what we will observe)
- Latency percentiles (P50, P95, P99) per route and per model variant
- Error rate (5xx and model-timeout) per minute and per deployment window
- Time-to-detect (mean time to alert) and time-to-engage (pager to ack) for high-severity alerts
- Customer-impact proxy (failed-api-rate * active-sessions)
- Progress metrics: % of features with covenant signed, % of runbooks linked in deploy PRs

Stakeholders and roles
- Covenant sponsor: Asha Patel (SRE lead)
- Product liaison: Priya Rao (Product — Hosted API)
- Feature team leads: Diego Huang (Embeddings), Noah Kim (Routing)
- Observability owner: Maya R. Singh (Observability)
- Oncall experiment facilitators: rotating SREs (see experiment schedule)

Covenant commitments (short, two-way)
- Feature teams commit to: include a short "operational contract" in PRs (one paragraph) describing expected latency and failure modes, link to a single runbook, and identify a primary owner for 30 days post-launch.
- SRE commits to: provide a lightweight readiness review (15–30m) for feature owners before rollout; ensure alert templates and a temporary mitigation (circuit, fallback) are available; run the experiment facilitation and capture lessons.

30/60/90 experiments (overview)
- 30d (Quick fire): Mandatory operational paragraph in PRs + tagging runbook. Outcome: measure compliance rate and capture friction.
- 60d (Handoff dress rehearsal): Simulated incident drill focused on crossover between feature owner and oncall. Outcome: mean time-to-engage and handoff friction points.
- 90d (Partial SLO pilot): For 2 services, define a trial-level objective (target P95 latency window & error budget rules), expose dashboards in Console, and run a live canary rollback policy. Outcome: feasibility of full SLO rollout and cost/ops tradeoffs.

Decision points and success criteria
- Accept experiment as "green" if compliance > 80% for PR operational paragraphs and runbook linkage by day 30.
- Accept handoff flow if mean time-to-engage under 10m in 3 of 4 drills.
- Consider scaling partial SLO pilot if customer-impact proxy improves by >=20% without >10% ops overhead.

Meeting cadence and coordination
- Weekly 30m sync (Mon 11:00) for the first 6 weeks — status, blockers, short experiments retrospective.
- Post-incident debrief template to be used within 48h for any drill/incidents during the experiments.

Runbooks and quick-run checklist (to be linked in PRs)
- One-paragraph operational contract (template below).
- Runbook link + minimal recovery steps (fallback route, disable feature flag, rollback PR link).
- Owner contact and secondary.

Template: Operational contract (paste in PR description)
- Expected steady-state latency: < 120ms P95
- Expected failure modes: model-timeout (>=500ms), upstream-rate-limit (429s).
- Temporary mitigation: disable experimental routing or use cached embeddings; owner: @last-name.

Risks / open questions
- Which services are highest leverage for the 90d pilot? (Triage candidates: routing, embeddings ingest, chat front-end).
- Alert noise: we must filter low-actionability signals before drills to avoid fatigue.
- Legal / customer comms: when do we externally commit to an objective? Keep pilot internal.

Dependencies
- Observability: must expose per-route percentiles and error budgets in Console (Maya to scope).
- Release engineering: ability to gate rollouts with the one-paragraph contract (Diego to prototype gating label).

Next actions (owners and due dates)
- Asha: draft PR template + link in repo templates (2026-06-18).
- Maya: surface dashboard proto for two candidate services (2026-06-25).
- Diego: add PR lint rule to encourage covenant paragraph (2026-06-22).
- Priya: pick 2 candidate features for the pilot (2026-06-20).

Notes to self / working thoughts
- Keep language simple so product PMs will sign.
- Focus on experiments that reduce ops feedback loop time, not on heavy instrumentation first.
- Expect cultural friction; capture 5 non-obvious blockers after each drill.

Appendix: quick logs (experiment snapshots)
- 2026-06-20: kickoff note — 7 teams volunteered for PR paragraph experiment.
- 2026-06-27: first compliance sweep — 42% of PRs included operational paragraph (actions: automated comment + link to template).
- 2026-06-30: drill #1 — simulated partial outage on embeddings ingest; time-to-detect 4m, time-to-engage 18m (owner not paged due to mis-tagged rotation). Learning: ensure roster tags are up to date in PagerDuty/Slack.

Unresolved items to capture in meetings
- Exact template fields to surface in Console from runbooks (short bullets only).
- Mechanism for product sign-off — checkbox in PR? lightweight doc signature?

End.
